newsitem.title: UK: Shetland Islands welcome new BP oil discovery.
newsitem.headline: Shetland Islands welcome new BP oil discovery.

text.p: The discovery by British Petroleum Co Plc (BP) of a new oilfield west of the Shetlands could ensure the future of the islands' Sullom Voe terminal, an official said on Monday.
"It's very good news," said Alastair Cooper, divisional manager of resources for the Shetland Islands Council (SIC).
"As far as the Shetlands are concerned, the more oil they find the more likelihood of a pipeline coming to land and if that happens we will be bidding hard for it," he told Reuters.

BP said on Monday it had discovered an oilfield 100 miles west of the islands in block 204/19. In response, the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) said it would offer two new blocks for exploration to the north of the find.
"We were aware there was a lot of exploration activity last year and we're glad a piece of good news has come out of it. We think there will be more activity this year," said Cooper.

Earlier this year the Sullom Voe terminal, which employs 800-1,200 people out of a population of 22,000 and which loads world benchmark Brent Blend crude oil onto tankers, won a tender to handle oil from BP's second Atlantic Margin field, Schiehallion, when it comes on stream in mid-1998.

Brent volumes are expected to decline dramatically by the turn of the century and oil from Foinaven, BP's first field west of the islands, will be handled by the Flotta terminal on the Orkney Islands when it starts to flow in April.
"Schiehallion alone is not enough to ensure the future of Sullom Voe terminal long term so the more they find the better it is for us," Cooper said.
